question: Not shared at the level of population class. Both papers detect current MoCA-defined MCI (MoCA < 26 in P-339; MoCA <= 26 in P-19) from clinical and questionnaire tabular data, so the task and channel match. The populations behind the label differ in kind. P-339 studies hospitalised type 2 diabetes patients aged 40-75 in an endocrinology department. P-19 studies working-age coal miners with occupational dust exposure (inclusion age >= 18; mean age 42.6 in the normal group and 48.8 in the MCI group) attending an occupational health examination. Each model is built on predictors tied to its population's defining condition: the Chinese visceral adiposity index in P-339; work years, social support and anxiety scores in P-19. Neither sample is a subset of the other's population. P-339 itself states that findings from other populations have limited relevance to people with diabetes.

figures.P-339: Nomogram (age, gender, education, CVAI), 95% CIs as printed. Training, apparent (n = 236; 109 MCI/127 NC): 0.765 [0.705, 0.826]. Random 30% validation (n = 101; 49 MCI/52 NC): 0.690 [0.588, 0.792]. Optimism-corrected C-index 0.747 [0.695, 0.800]. A Hanley-McNeil check reproduces the printed validation interval: Q1 = 0.5267, Q2 = 0.5634, SE = 0.0528, [0.587, 0.793].
figures.P-19: No AUC interval printed (validation Table 4 gives fold SDs: XGBoost 0.79 (0.01), Logistic 0.81 (0.02)). XGBoost: training 0.959, validation 0.795, separately recruited test set 0.913. Logistic: 0.818 / 0.816 / 0.778. Derived Hanley-McNeil intervals. Test set (50 MCI, 301 normal), XGBoost 0.913: Q1 = 0.8399, Q2 = 0.8715, SE^2 = 11.764/(50*301), SE = 0.0280, CI [0.858, 0.968]; Logistic 0.778: SE = 0.0403, CI [0.699, 0.857]. Validation set (8:2 split, n = 388; about 66 MCI and 322 normal at the cohort's 331/1938 prevalence), XGBoost 0.795: SE = 0.0344, CI [0.728, 0.862]; Logistic 0.816: SE = 0.0331, CI [0.751, 0.881]. Logistic training (n = 1550, about 265/1285) 0.818: CI [0.786, 0.850].

matched_figure_check: Neither paper reports a result in the other's population or on the other's predictor set, so no matched figure removes the population difference. Held-out comparisons: P-339's validation 0.690 [0.588, 0.792] against P-19's XGBoost test 0.913 [0.858, 0.968] differs both ways; against P-19's XGBoost validation 0.795 [0.728, 0.862] it also differs both ways, narrowly (0.795 lies 0.003 above P-339's upper bound). On the same model class (logistic regression) the figures partly agree: P-19's logistic test AUC 0.778 lies inside P-339's validation interval, though 0.690 lies just below P-19's [0.699, 0.857]; P-19's logistic training AUC 0.818 lies inside P-339's training interval [0.705, 0.826], though 0.765 lies below P-19's [0.786, 0.850]. The recorded gap (0.765 apparent training against 0.913 test) is not dissolved by a matched figure, but it mixes validation stages, and most of it follows the XGBoost-against-logistic difference.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply to the compared figures (0.765, 0.690, 0.913, 0.795). P-19's random-forest training AUC of 0.981 would meet the near-ceiling level, but it is an apparent training value and not a compared figure.
reason: The numbers differ beyond uncertainty (P-19's XGBoost test AUC 0.913 lies outside both of P-339's printed intervals), and no matched figure reconciles them. But the two AUCs describe MCI detection in different population classes: hospitalised adults with type 2 diabetes against working-age dust-exposed coal miners, each with predictors chosen for its own population's defining condition. So the pair fails condition 1. The record also cites P-339's apparent training AUC (0.765) rather than its validation AUC (0.690).

quotes.quote: Moreover, most research has focused on elderly or non-diabetic populations, limiting its relevance to individuals with diabetes.

Patients with T2DM who were admitted to the Department of Endocrinology at the Affiliated Zhongda Hospital of Southeast University between November 2021 and April 2023 were consecutively enrolled in this study.
MoCA score ≥ 26 is considered normal (NC group) and MoCA score <26 is considered MCI(MCI group)
with AUC values of 0.765 (95% CI: 0.705–0.826) in the training cohort and 0.690 (95% CI 0.588–0.792) in the validation cohort (Fig. 4C, D).
Workers exposed to dust who underwent health examinations at the Occupational Health Examination Center from May 2022 to October 2022 were selected as research subjects.
A total score of ≤26 is considered to indicate that there may be mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and a total score of > 26 is defined as a normal population.
A total of 1938 miners were included, of which 1607 were in the normal group with an average age of 42.642 (7.254) years

XGBoost (training set: AUC=0.959, validation set: AUC=0.795) and Logistic Regression (training set: AUC=0.818, validation set: AUC=0.816) models exhibited superior predictive performance. Results from the test set showed that the AUC of the XGBoost model (AUC=0.913) outperformed the Logistic Regression model (AUC=0.778).
In this test set, there were 301 people in the normal group with an average age of 43.6years
